newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-WAUGH SAYS MATCH-WINNING CENTURY HIS BEST YET.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH SAYS MATCH-WINNING CENTURY HIS BEST YET.

text.p: Mark Waugh, who steered Australia to a two-wicket win in the second test against South Africa on Monday, said he considered his 116 to be the best of his 11 test centuries.

"My hundred (126) in Jamaica comes pretty close but this was definitely the best," Waugh said. "The conditions were difficult and it was always going to be difficult to score 270 on this wicket. I'm very, very happy indeed."
Australia beat West Indies at Jamaica in 1995 to regain the Frank Worrell Trophy. It was the first time West Indies had been beaten in a series since 1980.

For Australian captain Mark Taylor the victory must have been bitter-sweet. After playing his 17th and 18th successive test innings without a 50, he nevertheless led his side to their first series victory over South Africa since 1957-58.

"It's not up to me or the players to say that we are the best. The scribes can say that and hand out titles. But I'm delighted with the way we are playing our cricket and as long as we keep winning test matches and series then I can't be happier," Taylor said.
"This is the best victory I have ever experienced with Australia. It's even better than Jamaica."

Despite increasing speculation that Taylor may be forced to drop himself, the captain remains determined to stay. "I'm captain of Australia and I am going to do the job for as long as I can. I'll definitely be playing in the third test next week. I have no plans to drop myself."

Coach Geoff Marsh fully supported Taylor: "He's a tougher man than you and I. We are all 100 percent behind him. Every day we do as much as we can to help him. The way he carries himself in the dressing room is unbelievable because he is so disappointd with his own form," Marsh said.
Hansie Cronje was fulsome in his praise for Australia and, particularly, for Waugh.

"I can't heap enough praise on him. It was a fantastic innings in difficult conditions. He was the difference between the teams during this test. We had our chances and, with a little more luck on the last morning, I thought we could have turned it ou way.
"Allan Donald bowled magnificently in both innings and took just one wicket," Cronje said.

Waugh, too, praised Donald. "He was brilliant. He deserved more but, that's cricket. Jason Gillespie bowled well too and he took a bundle (eight for 103 in the match). I'm sure Allan will be running in just as hard next week and maybe he'll have more luck."
